pests.name: Aphids
pests.note_beginner: Small soft insects that cluster on new growth. Ironically, sweet alyssum is best known for attracting the hoverflies and tiny wasps whose young eat aphids, so light infestations often take care of themselves. A strong spray of water or insecticidal soap handles heavier ones.
pests.note_seasoned: Soft-bodied sap-feeders on tender growth; usually minor on sweet alyssum, whose own draw of syrphid flies and parasitoids tends to suppress them. Hose off or treat with insecticidal soap only if colonies build, and conserve the natural enemies the plant attracts.

pests.name: Flea beetles
pests.note_beginner: Tiny dark beetles that jump when disturbed and chew small round holes in leaves. Because sweet alyssum is in the cabbage family, it can attract them, especially near cole crops. Floating row cover on seedlings and healthy, vigorous plants usually keep damage cosmetic.
pests.note_seasoned: As a Brassicaceae member, sweet alyssum can host flea beetles, which shot-hole the foliage; damage is usually cosmetic on an established carpet. Protect seedlings with row cover where pressure is high, and note the shared-pest overlap when interplanting near cole crops.

pests.name: Cabbage-family caterpillars
pests.note_beginner: Caterpillars such as cabbage white larvae sometimes chew the leaves. Pick them off, or use a targeted Bt product if there are many.
pests.note_seasoned: Larvae of cabbage whites and related brassica-feeding caterpillars occasionally graze the foliage; usually cosmetic on sweet alyssum. Hand-pick or apply Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) where populations warrant, and monitor when it is interplanted with cole crops.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.note_beginner: In cool, damp weather these chew ragged holes in the low foliage, mostly at night. Hand-pick after dark, set traps, or use iron-phosphate bait, and clear damp hiding spots near the plants.
pests.note_seasoned: Slugs and snails rasp holes in the low, dense canopy under damp, mild conditions. Reduce harborage, hand-pick at night, and use traps or iron-phosphate baits; pressure is highest in shaded, mulched, irrigated plantings.

diseases.name: Stem, crown, and root rot
diseases.note_beginner: The most common way sweet alyssum is lost. Plants wilt, yellow, and collapse from the base, usually because the soil stayed wet or drained poorly. Plant in well-drained soil, do not overwater, and do not crowd plants into soggy beds.
diseases.note_seasoned: Sweet alyssum's signature weakness: stem and crown/root rots favored by wet, poorly drained soil, which collapse the plant at the base and cause outright decline in soggy beds. Management is cultural, excellent drainage, restrained watering, and airflow; very good drainage is essential for good performance.

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.note_beginner: A disease that shows as yellowing above and a grayish fuzz on the underside of leaves, worst in cool, wet, crowded conditions. Space plants for airflow and keep the foliage dry.
diseases.note_seasoned: Cool, wet, crowded conditions favor downy mildew, with yellowing above and sporulation beneath. Manage with spacing for airflow, base watering in the morning, and sanitation of infected debris.

diseases.name: Damping-off
diseases.note_beginner: Seedlings sometimes rot at the soil line and topple over soon after sprouting, usually in cold, wet, overplanted conditions. Sow into a clean, well-draining mix, do not overwater, and give seedlings light and air.
diseases.note_seasoned: A seedling-stage collapse at the soil line driven by cold, saturated, overcrowded conditions and soilborne fungi. Sow thinly into a clean, free-draining medium, avoid overwatering, and provide light and airflow; the same drainage discipline that limits the crown rots limits this.
